subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a parent-side delegate-only/self-deny config contract, and if so should it be `selfDeny`, `delegateOnly`, scoped allow entries, or part of the per-spawn `toolsAllow` design?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change defines who may see or invoke exec/write/edit across parent and child sessions, so automation should not choose the permanent security and config contract.

options.title: Design delegate-only as a core policy
options.body: Add a documented per-agent delegate-only/self-deny contract that hides tools from the parent while allowing explicitly configured child inheritance, with deny-wins tests and docs.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn toolsAllow
options.body: Require callers to use per-spawn child allowlists and leave parent direct-use prevention to separate agent profiles or instructions, accepting that this does not solve all reports here.

options.title: Defer until diagnostics land
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers first add declared/effective tool visibility and clipping reasons, then revisit enforcement once operators can inspect the result.

recommendation.title: Design delegate-only as a core policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented per-agent delegate-only/self-deny contract that hides tools from the parent while allowing explicitly configured child inheritance, with deny-wins tests and docs.
